title: Add audit-export health endpoints + per-destination status fields (last_success_at, last_error, backlog_estimate)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
Expose a stable, customer- and Console-consumable view of audit export health.

We need (a) dedicated health endpoints for the exporter pipeline and (b) per-destination status fields on destination CRUD responses, so Console can render destination health states and Support/SRE can quickly triage issues without digging through internal dashboards.

Context
SIEM-ready audit export (beta) supports sinks: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, S3. Delivery semantics are at-least-once. Customers will see duplicates; we should make delivery health explicit (including backlog) and provide clear error surfaces.

Scope
1) API fields for destination status
- Add these status fields to destination responses (GET destination, LIST destinations, and create/update response payloads):
  - last_success_at (RFC3339 timestamp; null if never succeeded)
  - last_attempt_at (RFC3339 timestamp; optional but strongly recommended for UX)
  - last_error (string; null if none)
  - last_error_at (RFC3339; null if none)
  - backlog_estimate (integer count of queued audit events pending delivery for this destination; may be approximate)
  - health_state (enum: healthy | degraded | failing | paused | disabled)
  - state_reason (string; short machine-friendly reason, e.g., "auth_failed", "sink_throttled", "dlq_growth", "paused_by_operator")

Notes:
- The ticket title mentions last_success_at / last_error / backlog_estimate; we should include last_error_at + health_state to avoid ambiguous "red/green" logic in Console and to support paging thresholds.
- All fields must be safe to display to customer admins (no credential material; no internal hostnames). "last_error" should be sanitized and provide an error_id for Support correlation.

2) Health endpoints
- Provide a lightweight endpoint for Console polling / human triage:
  - GET /v1/audit-exports/health
    Returns overall exporter health and summary counts (e.g., destinations_healthy/degraded/failing), plus global backlog.
  - GET /v1/audit-exports/destinations/{destination_id}/health
    Returns destination-specific status including fields above, plus last_delivered_event_at if available.

If endpoint naming needs to align with existing control plane conventions, propose alternates in implementation notes and get Chloe/Felix sign-off.

3) Data model + update source of truth
- Control plane should persist status per destination. Source of truth is the delivery worker subsystem (worker writes periodic status updates keyed by destination_id + tenant/workspace).
- Define update cadence:
  - Worker publishes status at least every 60s while enabled, and on error transitions.
  - If status is stale (no update for >5 minutes), control plane should mark health_state=degraded with reason="stale_status".

4) Error taxonomy
- last_error must be consistent across sinks (Splunk/Datadog/S3). Normalize into:
  - category: auth | throttling | network | sink_5xx | schema | config | unknown
  - retryable: true/false

Since we cannot return nested objects, encode as a single string with a stable format, e.g.:
"category=auth retryable=false error_id=ae_01J... message=Splunk token rejected (401)"

Out of scope
- Full replay tooling (tracked in ENG-13934)
- Deep per-event trace links in the customer API (we can add later)
- Customer-configurable alerting from within Console (GA feature)

Acceptance criteria
- Destination responses include last_success_at, last_error, backlog_estimate (and the additional recommended fields) and are exercised by unit + integration tests.
- Health endpoints exist, are documented in internal API reference, and are consumed by Console backend (ENG-13929) without additional ad-hoc fields.
- backlog_estimate semantics documented: approximate, may lag, defined per destination within a tenant/workspace.
- last_error is sanitized and does not leak secrets or internal infrastructure identifiers.
- Migration/backfill behavior defined for existing destinations (null/0 defaults).

Implementation notes / questions
- backlog_estimate calculation:
  - Preferred: worker reports "queue_depth" from its durable queue partition for that destination.
  - Alternative: estimate from checkpoints (produced - delivered), but risk of negative/incorrect under replay.
- Multi-deployment:
  - Hosted/Dedicated: status lives in control plane DB.
  - Private: status endpoint should be served by the private control plane; worker must be able to write status updates within the private network.
- Rate limits:
  - Console will poll list + per-destination detail. Ensure endpoints are cheap and cacheable.

Links
- Project epic: ENG-13920
- Related work: ENG-13921 (destination model), ENG-13923 (queue/worker), ENG-13929 (Console backend)

Owner
Benji Okafor (Platform Control Plane)

Reviewers
- Felix Schneider (Console backend consumer)
- Sean Gallagher (SRE: alerting + health semantics)
- Marcus Lin (Security: error redaction expectations)
comments: 2025-02-06 (Ethan Park): Console needs a reliable health model for beta onboarding. Please include a coarse health_state enum; otherwise every consumer will reinvent logic based on null/nonnull last_error.
2025-02-07 (Chloe Martin): +1 on health_state. Also want last_attempt_at so we can show "trying" vs "stuck". Console design has states: Healthy / Degraded / Failing / Paused / Disabled.

2025-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): For paging, we care about (a) sustained failing destinations and (b) backlog growth beyond bounds. Please ensure backlog_estimate is defined per-destination and not just global queue depth. Also define staleness behavior if worker stops reporting.

2025-02-11 (Benji Okafor): Plan: worker publishes status to control plane every 60s + on transition. Control plane derives health_state with staleness rules. I’ll add last_error_at + error_id so Support can correlate to logs.

2025-02-13 (Marcus Lin): last_error must not include endpoint URLs, tokens, headers, or raw payloads. Please sanitize messages and cap length (e.g., 512 chars). If needed, include an error_id for internal lookup.

2025-02-18 (Felix Schneider): For list views, we only need the summary fields (health_state, last_success_at, backlog_estimate, last_error). Detail endpoint can include last_attempt_at + last_error_at. Please keep response stable for beta docs.
activity_log: 2025-02-05: Issue created by Ethan Park; scoped to per-destination status + health endpoints.
2025-02-11: Updated scope to include health_state + staleness rules based on SRE feedback.
2025-02-18: Added security sanitization requirements for last_error and error_id support.
